candidate.text: Prioritized plan returned as the structured artifact, with source IDs cited, the predecessor hash preserved, and two blocked stages disclosed.

data.summary: Prioritized implementation plan for the first release of the customer support portal: sign-in, then account recovery, then support request creation, then request status reading, with a release check gating on keyboard navigation and screen-reader support. Two stages remain blocked: account recovery acceptance criteria and the accessibility verification method.
claims: Scope is a first release of a customer support portal for existing customers; implementation has not started (context).
Required capabilities per the brief: sign in, recover an account, open a support request, read request status.
Accessibility is release-blocking: the first release must work with keyboard navigation and screen readers (brief).
Priority 1 is sign-in, since recovery and request flows depend on an authenticated identity.
Priority 2 is account recovery, blocked until its acceptance criteria are defined (outstanding).
Priority 3 is opening a support request; Priority 4 is reading request status, which depends on request creation.
Priority 5 is a release check covering keyboard navigation and screen-reader support across all four flows.
The accessibility verification method is undefined (outstanding), so the release check cannot yet be stated as a pass/fail gate.
New-customer registration is out of scope; brief and context cover existing customers only.
unresolved: Account recovery acceptance criteria are undefined, so that work item cannot be sized or accepted.
Accessibility verification method is undefined: tooling, assistive-technology matrix, and pass threshold are unspecified.
No stated recovery channel (email, phone, support-agent assisted) or identity-proofing bar for recovery.
No stated support-request fields, status values, or notification behavior for status reading.
No timeline, team capacity, or platform/browser targets given, so priority order is dependency-based rather than schedule-based.
